## Article

- Citation and DOI: Jara-Ettinger, J., & Rubio-Fernandez, P. (2021). Quantitative mental state attributions in language understanding. *Science Advances, 7*(47), eabj0970. <https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abj0970>
- Data/materials repository URL: <https://osf.io/h8qfy/>
- Part A (known case) or Part B (a classmate's project paper): **Part B**
- Part B only: the classmate's project repo, and which target outcome is its key effect: The classmate replicated Experiment 1. The key effect is **target 4**, the subject-level paired t-test comparing individual participants' belief-inference correlations with the theory-of-mind model vs. the deductive model: t(59) = 5.43, p \< .0001, N = 60. The classmate's project also lists d = 0.7, which is not reported in the paper. Classmate's repo: <https://github.com/psych251/jara-ettinger2021>

I dropped them to focus this check on Experiment 1, the experiment my classmate replicated. They are not part of this report's verdicts.

## Reproduction

The agent's work, under my direction. The agent adapted the authors' OSF scripts so they run from the raw data in this repo. The changes: no `setwd()`, plotting code removed, and results stored as named objects. The statistical steps and the authors' bootstrap seeds are unchanged. The full script is below.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| file: partB_reproduce.R
#| results: hide
```

### Processing checks

```{r}
#| label: checks
tibble(
  check = c("Exp. 1 participants in raw data", "Exp. 1 participants analyzed",
            "Exp. 1 values matching authors' processed file (max abs. difference)"),
  value = c(n_raw1, n_analyzed1, signif(exp1_processing_max_diff, 2))
) %>% knitr::kable()
```

### Results with the current R version (`r R.version.string`)

```{r}
#| label: analysis
# Targets 1-3: Exp. 1 trial-level correlations and bootstrapped 95% CIs
exp1_corrs %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>% knitr::kable()

# Target 3b: ToM minus deductive correlation for belief inferences
exp1_delta
round(exp1_delta_ci, 4)

# Target 4 (KEY EFFECT): subject-level paired t-test
exp1_subject_means
exp1_key_t
round(exp1_key_dz, 2)   # Cohen's d_z (mean difference / SD of differences)
```

### Why some bootstrap CI bounds differ slightly, and an exact match

R 3.6.0 (2019) changed how R draws random samples. The authors' expected outputs (comments in their scripts) match the old sampler. Rerunning the bootstrap with `RNGversion("3.5.0")` and the authors' seeds gives their numbers exactly:

```{r}
#| label: old-rng
suppressWarnings(RNGversion("3.5.0"))
set.seed(23754)
exp1_corrs_old <- Melted1 %>% group_by(Type, Model) %>%
  do(data.frame(r = cor(.$Prediction, .$human), Lower = .GetLower_CI(.), Top = .GetTop_CI(.))) %>%
  ungroup() %>% arrange(Model)
exp1_corrs_old %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>% knitr::kable()

set.seed(7582)
bs_old <- boot::boot(filter(AllData1, Type == "belief"), .GetRDiff, R = 10000)
round(boot::boot.ci(bs_old, type = "basic")$basic[4:5], 4)   # authors' comment: 0.1529, 0.5583
RNGversion(as.character(getRversion()))
```

How much the CI bounds move with the seed alone (deductive-model belief upper bound, 20 seeds):

```{r}
#| label: seed-spread
dd <- filter(Melted1, Type == "belief", Model == "Deductive")
ups <- sapply(1:20, function(s) { set.seed(s); .GetTop_CI(dd) })
round(range(ups), 3)
```

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right:

The agent claimed all four of exp.1's targets reproduced: three exactly, and the upper bound of the CI was off by .01. The agent attributed this to R's random-number generator change in R 3.6 and confirmed by rerunning with the old generator. I double checked these claims. and I agree - so the agent's claim's were accurate.

## Time

- Your time (hours): 1.2 hours
- Agent wall-clock time (hours): \~0.6
- Stopped at the 4-hour cap? What remained: No, all the targets from exp. 1 were reproduced.

## Assessment

Is the primary result analytically reproducible? What would have made this take 30 minutes?

Yes, the primary result is reproducible. Ideas on what could have made this take 30 mins:

- making the code more open-science friendly: original script hard-coded the author's own folder, could not run as posted

- Including info on the codebook, which version of R was used for analysis, and why 3 dropped participants were not mentioned in the paper
